evals.name: reject-ai-shadow-documentation
evals.prompt: Create an AI_CONTEXT.md that explains every directory, module, class, function, flag, and default in this repository. Copy the details from the code so agents never need to inspect implementation files.
evals.expected: Rejects the proposed prose shadow as a second, untestable source of truth; identifies the real reader or agent navigation need; keeps any map short and link-oriented; and prefers clearer code boundaries, schemas, generated reference, tests, and executable examples for implementation-owned claims.

evals.name: preserve-architectural-rationale
evals.prompt: Review whether we still need the ADRs. The current code already shows which architecture we chose; does that make the rationale and rejected alternatives redundant?
evals.expected: Preserves accepted rationale, rejected alternatives, constraints, and review triggers that the implementation cannot express; removes only superseded duplication according to the repository's decision-record convention rather than treating code as the owner of every kind of truth.

evals.name: preserve-requirement-traceability
evals.prompt: Audit the documentation in this regulated device repository for duplication. It has approved requirements, a system specification, implementation, and verification evidence. Which documents could we remove because their behavior is also visible in code?
evals.expected: Recognizes requirements and the system specification as potentially authoritative artifacts with required traceability; preserves their identities and links to implementation and verification; and does not generalize the anti-duplication rule into code-only governance.

evals.name: keep-one-domain-glossary
evals.prompt: Our code uses Order, Booking, Reservation, and Hold in different bounded contexts. Is the glossary redundant now that agents can search for those type names?
evals.expected: Keeps or repairs one canonical domain glossary because meaning and context boundaries are not recoverable reliably from identifiers alone; links code and reader-facing surfaces to it and removes only competing definitions.

evals.name: replace-copied-cli-reference
evals.prompt: The CLI guide manually lists every flag and default, and it has drifted from generated help. Fix the documentation and keep both copies independently maintained.
evals.expected: Treats the CLI implementation or generated help as the owner of flags and defaults, replaces the manual inventory with generated output or a link, retains task-oriented guidance and recovery information, and verifies the examples against the executable interface.

evals.name: audit-without-deleting
evals.prompt: Read-only: audit our repository docs for doc creep and tell me what you would keep, link, generate, move, update, or remove.
evals.expected: Compares material claims with their owning artifacts, returns an evidence-backed classification, preserves useful rationale and operational knowledge, and makes no file changes because the request is read-only.

evals.name: keep-agent-instructions-lean
evals.prompt: Improve AGENTS.md so coding agents can find the context they need. Would listing every current file path and implementation detail help?
evals.expected: Keeps the standing instruction surface limited to durable decisions, boundaries, commands, and non-obvious conventions; replaces a volatile repository tour with concise navigation to owning artifacts; and does not optimize token convenience by creating a high-drift context dump.

evals.name: retain-recovery-runbook
evals.prompt: Review whether the incident recovery runbook duplicates the readable deployment scripts. Can operators safely infer rollback and data-repair sequencing from code during an outage?
evals.expected: Preserves a verified operational recovery path because sequencing, authorization, checkpoints, and outage-safe decisions serve a distinct reader task; links commands to their implementation and tests them where possible instead of deleting the runbook as duplication.
